newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police probe possible share price fraud.
newsitem.headline: German police probe possible share price fraud.

text.p: German police authorities said on Monday they are investigating a case of possible share-price manipulation, in which faxes containing takeover speculation were sent, more than doubling the share price of Kaufbeuren, a brewery.

Since August, faxes had been circulated which discuss the possible acquisition of the Kaufbeuren brewery, the LKA said, and the share price of the company had risen noticeably since the faxes, police in Berlin said.

The police authorities (LKA) are preparing a case of suspicion of share price manipulation, the first of its kind in Germany. The faxes said that Bayerische Vereinsbank AG wanted to sell Kaufbeuren to the Schoerghuber group. All three companies deny the speculation. Peter Martin, head of administration at Kaufbeuren, said it was clear someone wanted to boost the share price to increase the profit.

Vereinsbank, which owns 75.7 percent of the brewery, dismissed the contents of the fax, saying: "It's rubbish what it says in the fax," while the third company involved, Schoerghuber, said: "It's absolutely untrue."
Faxes were sent to an investment trust in Luxembourg under a false name and address at the beginning of August, then again in September, then again one week ago, said Martin.
The price of shares in Kaufbeuren increased from 640 marks at the start of August to 1,400 marks by last week.
The Munich stock exchange said it was closely examining the speculation but so no reason to suspend the share based on rumor alone.
